newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian judge postpones Rao hearing until Oct 9.
newsitem.headline: Indian judge postpones Rao hearing until Oct 9.

text.p: An Indian judge on Monday postponed a criminal court hearing involving former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao until October 9.
Judge Ajit Bharihoke told the lower court that he was delaying the hearing following a Supreme Court ruling earlier on Monday exempting Rao from appearing in the court due to security threats.

The Supreme Court said that on October 7 it would consider a police request for the lower court hearing to be shifted to a more secure location. The hearing was to examine allegations that Rao conspired to cheat a businessman of $100,000. Rao says he is innocent.
The high court exempted Rao from appearing in the Tis Hazari court complex in central Delhi after police warned of the possibility of militant attacks against the former prime minister.
Pallav Sisodia, a lawyer representing the Central Bureau of Investigation, said the government was aiding Rao. "The government of India is helping the accused," Sisodia told Judge Bharihoke.
But Rao's counsel said the political leader was under threat. "Terrorism is the biggest threat for Mr Rao in New Delhi," lawyer R.K. Anand told reporters.
